lines.text: Many learners say: The pizza is too tasty.
Better: The pizza is very tasty.
Too means more than you want.
Very! The cake is very tasty.

data.why: Too means more than you want.

quiz.stem: The cake is ___ tasty. I love it.

native.tip: 한국어 “너무 맛있다”의 “너무”는 “아주”라는 뜻으로 쓰이지만, too는 “지나치게”라서 부정적이에요. “very tasty”!

en.tip: Korean “neomu” means very, but English too means more than good. Say “The pizza is very tasty”.
en.caption: Do you say “The pizza is too tasty”? 😅 Too sounds like a problem. To praise, use very. “The pizza is very tasty” is right. Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.
